Point P is marked at the center grid point of the square. Reasoning: Q is randomly selected from the 80 points excluding P. For line PQ to be an axis of symmetry of the square, it must be an axis of symmetry passing through the center of the square. The square has 4 such axes of symmetry: the horizontal midline, the vertical midline, and the two diagonals. method.method_draft: Use a direct symmetry-axis count. From the image, note that the square contains a 9-by-9 uniformly spaced grid of points and that P is the center grid point. From the text, Q is chosen from the other 80 grid points. A square has exactly four lines of symmetry through its center: the horizontal midline, vertical midline, and the two diagonals. In the 9-by-9 grid, each of these four lines contains 9 grid points, including P. Excluding P, each line contributes 8 possible choices for Q. These four sets overlap only at P, which is not allowed, so the number of favorable Q points is 4*8=32. The probability is 32/80=2/5.
